- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to match sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is strongly bearish (≤ -0.33) in recent days, model tends to overreact — reduce forecast slightly to avoid excessive downside.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in sentiment — cap forecast peak at 1–2% below true peak.  
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon — add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if recent 5-day average is trending upward.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model tends to lag — forecast should be adjusted upward by 0.5–1.0% to capture delayed momentum.  
- In 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period spikes — add 1–2% upward adjustment if sentiment turns bullish within last 3–5 days.
